source.authors: Gao Jin; Xinping Yi; Wei Huang; Sven Schewe; Xiao-Wei Huang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The title is truncated in the supplied metadata, but the paper title is readable in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures the train/test gap for adversarial robustness in adversarially trained classifiers, a distinct setting from the claim versions’ natural-label generalization results. It reports how its regularizer changes that robust gap.
record.gate_note: The reported train/test PGD-20 gaps concern adversarial accuracy, not the natural-label test error or the specific properties named in V1–V8. The clean and robust accuracy comparisons elsewhere in the paper do not separately measure the train/test gap.
record.test_reason: Section V-A uses sharpness-based weight sampling, citing original sources for V5 and V7, to evaluate S2O's weight statistics. It does not test any V1–V8 proposition. Robust generalization bounds and improvements from a new regularizer alone do not establish the specific comparisons those versions name.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: incorporating second-order weight statistics improves robustness and generalization, both with vanilla adversarial training and with other adversarial-training methods. This is their overall conclusion, not a uniform improvement across every coefficient and attack metric.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adversarial training and a second-order statistics regularizer; reports robust adversarial accuracy, rather than the claim versions’ natural-label generalization measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported robust train/test PGD-20 gap varies with the S2O coefficient α: 9.56 for AT and 8.17, 6.39, 5.68, 5.12, and 5.49 for α=0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4.

fits_no_version.finding: Table VII reports PGD-20 train/test gaps of 9.56 percentage points for AT and 8.17, 6.39, 5.68, 5.12, and 5.49 with increasing S2O coefficients. Both training and test accuracy change; a smaller gap alone does not establish improved test robustness under every evaluation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: S2O reduces the PGD-20 train/test accuracy gap for adversarially trained PreAct ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 across the tested coefficients.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The gap evidence is limited to one architecture, dataset, threat model, and attack metric in the sensitivity table; no uncertainty estimates are reported there. The measured robust gap does not establish the natural-label generalization claims in the versions.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported train/test gap results beyond Table VII were identified. Other tables report clean or adversarial test accuracy, not the train/test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal with weight decay.

Whether magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance ranks generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks better than norm and margin measures. Figure 4 measures correlation-matrix statistics, not this relationship.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and measuring retrained test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows. The decisive issue is the absence of the comparisons specified in V1–V8, not merely the use of adversarial accuracy. Sharpness-based sampling and PAC-Bayesian bounds do not themselves test V7's empirical ranking claim. The method-performance rows belong under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on natural-label test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Large-batch effects on natural-label held-out performance under epoch budgets.
Dropout effects on natural-label held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to natural-label train/test generalization gaps.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on natural-label test accuracy.
